narrative.overview: Medusa TV is an editorial, zero-slop streaming interface built specifically for Android TV, living room displays, and OLED panels. Designed following the clean, content-first philosophies of Apple TV+ and Netflix, it rejects artificial cosmetic containers, decorative border noise, and fantasy prose in favor of pure cinematic art, strong focal hierarchy, and high-performance rendering.
keyCharacteristics: Zero Idle Border Slop: Clean obsidian glass surfaces with no 1px outline noise in resting state.
Inescapable 10-Foot Focus: High-contrast solid cyan focus with deep ink text (#06080D) readable from 3 meters.
Pure Full-Bleed Art: Movie and series cards are 100% photographic artwork with title and metadata displayed cleanly outside the poster on the dark ground plane.
Hardware-Friendly Performance: Flat alpha layers and compiled native gradients instead of GPU-heavy real-time blur.
Remote-First Navigation: Zero on-screen back buttons on TV; navigation relies naturally on the physical TV remote BACK key.

rules.name: The Single Beacon Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element owns the focus indicator at any given moment. Idle elements must never simulate focus or carry glowing accents.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: All glass, scrim, and layer treatments must be achieved using native color alphas and linear Brush gradients. Costly GPU blur shaders are strictly prohibited.

rules.name: The Marquee Reveal Rule
rules.body: Text that overflows its single-line boundary must execute a smooth continuous marquee autoscroll (repeatDelayMillis = 2000) exclusively when its parent card or button holds D-Pad focus. Resting text truncates cleanly with ellipsis.

rules.name: The Root-Scale Rule
rules.body: Zoom scaling (graphicsLayer { scaleX = ...; scaleY = ... }) and zIndex must be applied to the outer container root before any clipping or border modifiers. Scaling inside a clipped container causes badge and text cutoff.

dos: Do rely on the TV remote physical BACK key as the primary navigation mechanism for Android TV.
Do position title and metadata outside the poster boundary on the dark ground plane in vertical media rows.
Do illuminate the focused interactive element with solid Focus Cyan and deep #06080D text for 3-meter legibility.
Do dim non-focused cards in an active carousel to alpha = 0.65f to create an optical spotlight.
Do apply graphicsLayer scale and zIndex to the root container before any clip or border modifiers.
Do use basicMarquee(repeatDelayMillis = 2000) on long movie titles and episode descriptions when focused.
donts: Don't use real-time blur (Modifier.blur() or RenderEffect) anywhere in the app.
Don't draw 1px grey outline borders on cards, buttons, or chips in idle state (cero border slop).
Don't render on-screen [← Back] buttons in TV mode; TV users navigate via the remote.
Don't enclose vertical poster cards inside rigid grey boxes with static text beneath.
Don't clip badges or progress bars against card focus borders; always provide at least 10.dp internal breathing room.
Don't invent artificial drop shadows on dark backgrounds.
